canonical_data: agents, sessions, turns and their event streams, schedules and provider settings in SQLite (local mode) or Postgres with Redis (hosted mode)
current_repo_note: Repository created 2026-07-23, so the 0.177 version line reflects rapid changeset-driven releases rather than a long history. The benchmark in the docs compares TrueForge with two other harnesses on 14 tasks and is run by its maintainer.
strengths: Sandbox-as-tool keeps the agent loop and credentials on the server while code, file and shell work runs in an isolated environment created only when an agent needs one, so a sandbox crash does not lose conversation state

Human checkpoints are built into the thread runtime: a tool call marked as requiring approval pauses the turn until the user allows or denies it, by default for MCP tools labelled write or destructive, and an ask-user-questions tool pauses for input
Sessions record turns, tool calls, subagents, tokens and timing, saved agents can run on a cron schedule, and everything is reachable through a documented HTTP API with TypeScript and Python SDKs
weaknesses: Daytona is the only sandbox provider supported today, so code execution depends on a third-party service, and the roadmap lists local sandbox execution as future work
Approval relies on MCP servers labelling tools: the docs warn that "Many servers skip labels, so those tools run without asking", and approve-once is still on the roadmap
Local mode has no login by default and the README says to keep it on localhost; shared use requires the hosted mode with Postgres and Redis
why_it_matters: A young but unusually complete open agent harness whose approval, sandbox and session model are documented and tested, a useful counterpart to hosted managed-agent runtimes.
